title: Sulphate-Based Zn, Fe and Cu Fertilization Modulates Growth and Yield of Wheat Varieties Under Contrasting Nutrient Management Strategies
content: Micronutrient deficiencies, particularly of zinc, iron and copper, constrain wheat productivity, and the choice of variety and micronutrient delivery method may influence crop performance. This study evaluated the effects of variety and micronutrient management on the growth, yield attributes and yield of wheat. A field experiment was conducted during 2022–23 and 2023–24 using two varieties (DBW-222 and HD-2967) and ten nutrient-management treatments comprising 100% recommended dose of fertilizer (RDF) alone or combined with Zn, Fe and Cu applied through soil or foliar application. Pooled analysis showed significant effects of variety and nutrient management on most traits. DBW-222 outperformed HD-2967, recording higher grain yield (6,139 vs. 5,249 kg ha⁻¹), biological yield (12,573 kg ha⁻¹) and harvest index (48.77%). Among treatments, soil application of Zn + Fe + Cu with 100% RDF (T8) gave the highest grain yield (6,284 kg ha⁻¹), biological yield (12,754 kg ha⁻¹), dry matter (1,845 g m⁻²) and harvest index (49.16%), whereas the control recorded the lowest grain yield (5,057 kg ha⁻¹). Foliar application of combined Zn + Fe + Cu (T9) was also superior to the control. In conclusion, DBW-222 was the more productive variety, and integrating soil-applied Zn, Fe and Cu with RDF provided the most consistent improvement in wheat growth and yield, while foliar application served as an effective supplementary option.
